red_flags.title: ITC cliff — BOC deadline already passed and no evidence provided
red_flags.evidence: Under OBBBA, the 30% solar ITC (~$30M+ on 100 MW) is forfeited unless physical-work BOC was documented by July 4, 2026 — a deadline already passed as of the research date. No BOC evidence package is in the dossier. This is the single largest go/no-go item; make BOC evidence a condition precedent.
red_flags.benchmark: BOC documented by Jul 4, 2026 (Notice 2025-42); continuity safe harbor → PIS by Dec 31, 2030

red_flags.title: SOAR voter-approval overlay is a potential kill-switch on ag/open-space land
red_flags.evidence: Ventura County's SOAR measures (A/B) require countywide voter approval to change land-use designations on protected agricultural and open-space land. A 100 MW solar farm on SOAR-protected farmland cannot be approved by the Board of Supervisors alone — it would need a ballot measure. This is the Ventura analog of the Solano 'zoning kill switch' and must be verified against the actual parcel. No SOAR status was provided.
red_flags.benchmark: Ag-protectionist counties prohibit commercial solar in ag districts; local route 18–36 mo with denial risk
sources: kb_lookup: zoning kill switch / ag-protectionist precedent

red_flags.title: Empty facts array — no site acreage, parcels, or zoning data supplied
red_flags.evidence: site_acres is null and no parcel APNs, zoning district, or SOAR status is given. A 100 MW solar+storage project typically needs ~600–700 acres (~6 ac/MWac). Without parcel/zoning/SOAR data, zoning feasibility and the entire entitlement path are unassessable.

red_flags.title: CEC Opt-In eligibility hinges on ≥200 MWh storage — storage size unstated
red_flags.evidence: 100 MW solar meets the ≥50 MW solar threshold, but Opt-In also requires storage ≥200 MWh. The project is labeled 'solar+storage' with no storage MWh given. If storage <200 MWh, the project is ineligible for the 270-day state certification that preempts local zoning — forcing the slower, litigation-prone local CEQA path.
red_flags.benchmark: Opt-In eligibility = solar ≥50 MW AND storage ≥200 MWh; CEC 270-day decision
sources: kb_lookup: CEC Opt-In Certification AB 205/AB 209 PRC §§25545–25545.9

red_flags.title: No permitting path or status provided
red_flags.evidence: The dossier contains no EIR status, no CEC Opt-In application, no permit stack. A 100 MW farmland project cannot proceed without a full EIR (12–24 mo) or a CEC Opt-In certificate (270 days). The permitting path is undetermined, which alone blocks any COD commitment.

red_flags.title: No biological/ecological survey data for a listed-species-rich county
red_flags.evidence: Ventura County supports multiple state/federally listed species (condor, least Bell's vireo, gnatcatcher, tiger salamander). No protocol surveys, species list, or habitat assessment was provided. Missing a seasonal survey window can add 6–12 months and freeze the layout.
red_flags.benchmark: Seasonal protocol surveys gate layout freeze; miss window → +6 months

red_flags.title: No community engagement, CBA, or AB 52 tribal consultation record
red_flags.evidence: No community benefits agreement, no AB 52 tribal consultation record, no engagement plan was provided. For the CEC Opt-In route a certified CBA is mandatory; for the local route, SOAR ag-preservation sentiment in Ventura makes farmland solar a high-opposition, high-litigation-risk proposition.
red_flags.benchmark: CBA ~$0.5–5M; AB 52 before EIR cert; ~43% plaintiff win rate
sources: kb_lookup: community CBA / AB 52 / litigation rate

red_flags.title: No financials provided — capex, PPA, and ITC status all unknown
red_flags.evidence: The facts array contains no capex, no PPA, no DSCR, no escalation reserve, no BOC evidence. Benchmark installed cost is $1.43–1.56/Wac (100 MW solar+storage ≈ $150–200M+). Without financials, bankability and the ITC cliff cannot be assessed.

red_flags.title: CAISO interconnection queue risk — no queue position or study provided
red_flags.evidence: Ventura is in SCE/CAISO territory. CAISO queue is >500 GW with only ~20% reaching COD; IR→COD ~5 years; Cluster 15 advanced only 145 of 541 projects. No queue position, cluster study, POI, or FCDS-vs-Energy-Only status was provided. Network-upgrade cost shock is the #1 dropout driver.
red_flags.benchmark: ~20% queue completion; 150% zonal intake cap; FCDS vs Energy-Only; ~30% post-screen attrition

red_flags.title: Transformer/GSU lead time is a hard schedule gate
red_flags.evidence: Large power transformers/GSUs carry 128–144 weeks (~2.5–2.8 yrs) lead time with ~30% national supply deficit. For any near-term COD, purchase orders had to be placed years in advance. No transformer PO or supply-chain plan was provided.
sources: kb_lookup: transformer lead time supply chain

red_flags.title: Grid integration — solar-only NQC is uneconomic; storage sizing is critical
red_flags.evidence: Standalone solar NQC ≈10% of nameplate and is ineligible for the new 6 GW CPUC procurement; 4-hr storage ≈90–95% NQC. Curtailment hit 11.5% of potential solar in early 2025; battery merchant revenue compressed to ~$52/kW-yr. Solar+storage is the only viable config, but the storage MWh is unstated — under-sizing storage destroys RA value.
red_flags.benchmark: Solar NQC ~10% / storage 90–95%; 11.5% curtailment; $52/kW-yr battery revenue

red_flags.title: No PPA/offtake — bankability and TPD allocation at risk
red_flags.evidence: No PPA, LOI, or offtake was provided. Bankability requires ≥80% of P50 contracted at financial close (executed PPA only, not LOI/MOU). CAISO PPA benchmark is $64.49/MWh (Q1-26, +13% YoY). Projects without executed PPAs nearly always withdraw from the CAISO queue.
red_flags.benchmark: PPA $64.49/MWh Q1-26; ≥80% of P50 contracted at FC; executed ≠ LOI

red_flags.title: Williamson Act incompatibility unresolved
red_flags.evidence: If any parcel is under a Williamson Act contract, commercial solar is an incompatible use. Exit requires 9-yr nonrenewal or cancellation at 12.5% of unrestricted FMV (25% for Farmland Security Zone). Ventura County has extensive contracted farmland; no WA status was provided.
red_flags.benchmark: WA cancellation at 12.5% of unrestricted FMV; 25% for Farmland Security Zone

red_flags.title: Gen-tie federal-land crossing unverified
red_flags.evidence: If the gen-tie crosses federal land (Los Padres National Forest, BLM, or near Naval Base Ventura County/Point Mugu), a ROW grant + NEPA review is triggered, adding ~2–3 years. No gen-tie route or federal-land interaction was provided.
red_flags.benchmark: BLM gen-tie crossing → ROW + NEPA + plan conformance; ~2–3 yrs precedent
sources: kb_lookup: BLM 2024 Western Solar Plan ROD

red_flags.title: BESS fire-safety permitting prerequisites unverified
red_flags.evidence: Storage requires fire-marshal sign-off under NFPA 855 / UL 9540A plus county building/electrical permits. No BESS spec, fire-marshal engagement, or UL 9540A listing evidence was provided.

red_flags.title: Coastal-zone and fire-hazard overlays unverified
red_flags.evidence: If any parcel lies in the coastal zone, Coastal Commission review is triggered; Ventura's high fire-hazard zones impose additional siting/vegetation-management constraints. No parcel location data was provided to rule these out.
red_flags.benchmark: Coastal Zone Management Act review; fire-hazard zone constraints

Provide integrated project schedule with NTP, COD, and all milestone dates, including permitting, construction, and commissioning.
Document beginning-of-construction (BOC) evidence for ITC/PTC eligibility, including physical work or 5% safe harbor, with dates and photographs.
Submit the full financial model with DSCR, escalation reserve, revenue assumptions, and sensitivity analysis.
Provide any community agreements, host community benefits, or opposition records.
List all permits obtained or pending, including conditional use permits, building permits, and environmental permits.

agency_actions.action: Verify zoning, land-use designation, SOAR overlay, and Williamson Act status for all parcels; initiate CEQA scoping if not already started.
agency_actions.why: Site control and land-use compatibility are critical; SOAR voter-approval overlay and Williamson Act restrictions could kill the project.

agency_actions.action: Confirm whether the storage component triggers CEC opt-in certification under AB 205 (≥200 MWh) and, if so, initiate CBA and prevailing wage compliance review.
agency_actions.why: AB 205 opt-in requires CEC certification and labor standards; failure to comply could delay or invalidate the project.

agency_actions.action: Verify interconnection queue position, study phase, and network upgrade cost allocation; obtain latest cluster study results.
agency_actions.why: Interconnection costs and timeline are major risks; CAISO queue delays and upgrade costs could materially affect CAPEX and schedule.

agency_actions.action: Confirm point of interconnection and any distribution-level upgrades required; obtain cost estimates and timeline.
agency_actions.why: SCE is the local utility and may have separate interconnection requirements beyond CAISO; cost and schedule exposure must be quantified.

verification_requests: Verify PPA with the offtaker: confirm contract execution, MW, price, escalation, tenor, and creditworthiness (e.g., investment-grade rating or parent guarantee).
Verify CAISO queue position and study results directly with CAISO (queue number, phase, and any cost allocation).
Verify supplier lead times for GSU transformers, modules, and BESS with manufacturers (e.g., confirm 128–144 week transformer lead time and any supply guarantees).
Verify BOC evidence with tax counsel: confirm physical work or 5% safe harbor documentation meets IRS requirements for ITC/PTC eligibility.
Verify EPC cost against benchmark bands ($1.43–1.56/Wac) using third-party cost indices (e.g., NREL, Lazard, or Wood Mackenzie).
Verify interconnection upgrade cost allocation with CAISO/SCE and compare to industry norms for similar projects.
conditions_precedent: All RFIs satisfied and documents reviewed; no material gaps in site control, permits, or contracts.
BOC evidence verified by tax counsel; ITC/PTC eligibility confirmed with no forfeiture risk.
Interconnection queue position and upgrade costs confirmed; total interconnection cost within acceptable threshold (e.g., <$50/kW).
Executed PPA with creditworthy offtaker; price and tenor within market benchmarks.
CAPEX within benchmark band ($1.43–1.56/Wac) including BESS and interconnection; contingency ≥10%.
CEQA and all environmental permits on track; no litigation risk that could delay COD beyond acceptable window.
Financial model validated with DSCR ≥1.30x and sensitivity analysis showing resilience to cost overruns and revenue shortfalls.
Equipment POs in place with delivery dates consistent with schedule; long-lead items (transformers) secured with deposits.
